decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display is a core-adjacent variant that costs little to keep in a broad display catalog, and with stable industry turnover there is no shortfall against aspiration that would trigger problemistic search.
The pegboard-back shelf display uses existing cardboard production capacity and serves hook-merchandise customers, so slack lets the firm carry it while demand evidence accumulates.
The standard quarter-pallet shelf display is a staple format for consumer brands and fits the firm's one-stop model closely, so it likely meets aspirations.
The eighth-pallet format complements the quarter-pallet line for smaller placements at low incremental cost, and nothing signals underperformance.
The wooden display pallet departs further from the cardboard core and carries more uncertainty, but one year is too early to judge it and slack in a large firm allows continued trial.
Demand for media-product displays is structurally declining, which raises the risk of shortfall, but the product is cheap to maintain in a close-to-core catalog and is likely kept for now.
